issue_asks: `#d {id}` with toc + attr_list must not raise TypeError
Must work with and without a [TOC] marker
A bare {id} should behave as if no id was given (generate normal slug)
Headings with real ids like {#my-id} must continue to work unchanged

findings.problem: This new test file largely duplicates the tests added to tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_toc.py. It also includes a test that re-runs other test modules from inside a test. This is redundant but harmless.
findings.evidence: The full suite passes: Ran 1185 tests, OK (skipped=52).

commands_run: python -c probe: '#d {id}', duplicate slugs with {id}, {id=}, {id=""}, setext heading with {id}, explicit-id collision, toc_depth config, md_in_html with a valueless id on a div
reviewer.summary: The fix is two small changes in toc.py. A valueless id (None) is now ignored when collecting used ids and counts as no id, so a slug is generated. The full suite passes. My own probes also behaved correctly: a bare {id} gets a unique slug next to duplicates and explicit ids, `{id=""}` still yields an empty id as before, and `{#my-id}` is untouched. Toc tokens, permalink and anchorlink output are correct. The attr_list output for a bare `{id}` without toc is unchanged. No tests were weakened. The only finding is a minor one: the new test file duplicates tests added elsewhere.

decision.why: every checklist item is true and there is no blocker/major finding
